exercise.name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl

reference.title: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.laterality: Unilateral, alternating (right then left in one loop)

breathing.pattern: Exhale on each curl, inhale as each dumbbell lowers.
breathing.cadence: Per arm: about 1.1 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.progression: Load is user-chosen: pick a dumbbell you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then weight.

cues.text: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in, thumbs forward.
Breathe out and curl the right dumbbell up and across toward the left chest, thumb up the whole way.
Squeeze with the dumbbell in front of the opposite chest; elbow stays low.
Lower it back down the same path to your right side.
Now the left: curl it across toward the right chest, thumb up.
Lower slowly to a straight arm.
Both arms straight; repeat, alternating sides.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting the trunk toward the dumbbell
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders and hips square to the front.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the elbow up and out
mistakes.fix: The elbow stays low and close; the forearm swings across.
Keep the thumb pointing up for the whole rep.
Take 2 s to lower each rep.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: Neutral (thumb up) the whole rep; the neutral grip shares the work with the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Upper arm stays close to the side and turns slightly inward as the forearm crosses the body (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

sources.title: GymVisual #029812, Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2023, biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy (Sports 11(3):64; PMC10054060)
Parpa, Vasiliou, Michaelides, Govindasamy, Chernov and Intziegianni 2025, biceps brachii EMG during traditional dumbbell versus Bayesian cable curls, with a review of curl EMG studies (Muscles 4:45)
Marcolin et al. 2018, differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl (PeerJ 6:e5165; PMC6047503)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: lighten the dumbbell and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm); a bent-back wrist under load strains the forearm (clinical opinion).
Pick the dumbbells up and set them down with a straight back and bent knees.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort crossing the body: curl straight up (hammer curl).
progressions: Both arms alternating without a pause.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Still a prime elbow flexor with the thumb up, though its activity was about 12% lower with a neutral grip than with a supinated grip (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Still a prime elbow flexor with the thumb up, though its activity was about 12% lower with a neutral grip than with a supinated grip (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) is best placed to flex the elbow with the thumb up; a review reported the hammer curl gave the highest brachioradialis activity among curls (Bagchi and Raizada 2019, as reviewed by Parpa 2025).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) is best placed to flex the elbow with the thumb up; a review reported the hammer curl gave the highest brachioradialis activity among curls (Bagchi and Raizada 2019, as reviewed by Parpa 2025).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder as the forearm swings across the body; neutral grips raised its activity versus supinated (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder as the forearm swings across the body; neutral grips raised its activity versus supinated (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.core: Resists the twist of one working arm; keep the trunk square.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Draws the upper arm slightly toward the midline as the dumbbell crosses the chest.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Draws the upper arm slightly toward the midline as the dumbbell crosses the chest.

phases.label: Arms at the sides, thumbs forward

guides.label: Right dumbbell curls across toward the left chest
Elbow bends through a full range
